source.title: Belfast Telegraph, 8 June 1967, p. 12 ("County of Antrim Notice of Result of Elections 1967")
source.publisher: Belfast Telegraph (via the British Newspaper Archive)
source.check: 24 divisions, 25 seats (Newtownabbey two): 5 contested (Ballycastle, Ballygomartin, Ballymena, Finaghy, Glenarm) and 19 unopposed, all named in the returning officer's notice of result. The notice prints no party labels; those shown for the contested divisions come from the Belfast Telegraph round-up of 2 June.

note: Election of the Antrim County Council, polled 1 June 1967 (Belfast Telegraph, 2 June 1967, p. 8, 'Round Up of the County Councils'). The returning officer's 'County of Antrim Notice of Result of Elections 1967' (Belfast Telegraph, 8 June 1967, p. 12), signed by W. S. Henderson, prints all 24 county electoral divisions: surname, other names, place of residence, votes recorded and names elected. It is the source for the unopposed returns, whose vote column is blank. Two seats. Kerr and McGowan both returned unopposed; the vote column is blank for both. The 2 June round-up printed no Newtownabbey contest. The four-candidate poll (Kerr 3,245; Robinson 3,152; Kidd 2,726; McMurtry 2,455) is the 4 June 1964 result recorded in 1964-06-04.json, not 1967. Returned unopposed.
